extracted.intended_audience: employers petitioning for CW-1 workers, CW-2 dependents, schools seeking SEVP certification/recertification, designated school officials (DSOs), and immigration practitioners
extracted.subtask_short: SEVP certification and CW nonimmigrant rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and adjudication standards for CNMI transitional worker (CW‑1/CW‑2) classification and for SEVP certification/recertification of schools to enroll F‑1 and M‑1 nonimmigrant students. Covers filing, documentation, recordkeeping, reporting, revocation, appeals, and site visit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of CW-1 status
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously maintained the terms and conditions of CW-1 status; remains admissible to the United States; and remains eligible for CW-1 classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are ongoing eligibility requirements the beneficiary must satisfy to be in CW-1 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on consecutive CW-1 petitions (three-period rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary (other than a long-term worker) may not be granted CW-1 status beyond three consecutive petition validity periods unless the beneficiary has departed and remained outside of the United States for a continuous period of at least 30 days after the expiration of the third petition validity period and before the filing of any new petition on behalf of the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits continuous use of CW-1 status; departure for at least 30 continuous days after the third period is required before a new petition may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW-2 extension dependent on CW-1 approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The derivative CW-2 nonimmigrant may file an application for extension of nonimmigrant stay on Form I-539 (or such alternative form as USCIS may designate) in accordance with the form instructions. The CW-2 status extension may not be approved until approval of the CW-1 extension petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW-2 extensions are administratively linked to the CW-1 petition approval; USCIS will not approve CW-2 extension until CW-1 extension is approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change or adjustment of status eligibility during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrant can apply to change nonimmigrant status under section 248 of the Act or apply for adjustment of status under section 245 of the Act, if otherwise eligible. During the transition period, CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrants may be the beneficiary of a petition for or may apply for any nonimmigrant or immigrant visa classification for which they may qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing for other classifications is permitted if statutory eligibility requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing for permanent residence does not preclude CW status
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may be granted, be admitted in and maintain lawful CW-1 or CW-2 nonimmigrant status while lawfully seeking to become a lawful permanent resident, provided he or she intends to depart the CNMI voluntarily at the end of the period of authorized stay. The filing or approval of a permanent labor certification, immigrant visa preference petition, or application for adjustment of status, or lack of residence abroad, will not be the basis for denying specified CW petitions, extensions, applications or admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will not deny CW petitions/extensions/applications/admission solely because the alien has pending immigrant petitions or lacks residence abroad, so long as the intent-to-depart-CNMI condition is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for numerical limits
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may reject an employer's petition for new or extended CW-1 status if any numerical limitation has been met. In that case, the petition and accompanying fee will be rejected and returned with the notice that numbers are unavailable for the CW nonimmigrant classification. The beneficiary's application for admission based upon an approved petition will not be rejected based upon the numerical limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection for lack of available numbers returns petition and fee; approved petitions are not retroactively invalidated for numerical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial and appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate decision to grant or deny CW-1 or CW-2 classification or status is a discretionary determination. The petition or application may be denied for failure to demonstrate eligibility or for other good cause. The denial of a petition to classify an alien as a CW-1 may be appealed to the USCIS Administrative Appeals Office or any successor body. The denial of CW-1 or CW-2 status within the CNMI, or of an application for change or extension of status filed under this section, may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between denials of petitions (appealable) and denials of status within CNMI or certain applications (not appealable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical limitations of CW status
rubrics_metrics.description: CW-1 and CW-2 statuses are only applicable in the CNMI. Entry, employment and residence in the rest of the United States (including Guam) require the appropriate visa or visa waiver and nonimmigrant classification. Except as provided, an alien with CW‑1 or CW‑2 status who enters or attempts to enter, or travels or attempts to travel to any other part of the United States without an appropriate visa or visa waiver, or who violates conditions of nonimmigrant stay applicable to any such authorized status in any other part of the United States, will be deemed to have violated CW‑1 or CW‑2 status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW status is geographically constrained to the CNMI; travel to other US parts without proper authority risks status violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-entry requirement to CNMI
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with CW-1 or CW-2 status who travels abroad from the CNMI will require a CW-1 or CW-2 or other appropriate visa to be re-admitted to the CNMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel outside CNMI requires appropriate visa for re‑admission to CNMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Guam transit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with CW-1 or CW-2 status may travel to a foreign place via a direct Guam transit without being deemed to violate that status. An alien with a valid CW-1 or CW-2 visa, admissible to the CNMI, may be admitted in Guam for the purpose of a direct Guam transit to the CNMI. An alien who violates the terms of direct Guam transit violates his or her CW status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited direct transit via Guam; violation of transit terms constitutes status violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with CW-1 nonimmigrant status is only authorized employment in the CNMI for the petitioning employer. An alien with CW-2 status is not authorized to be employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CW-1 employment is employer‑specific and geographically limited; CW-2 is not work-authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration triggers for CW status
rubrics_metrics.description: CW-1 status expires when the alien violates his or her CW-1 status (or in the case of a CW-1 status violation caused solely by termination of the alien's employment, at the end of the 30 day period described elsewhere), 10 days after the end of the petition's validity period, when the petition is revoked, or at the end of the transitional worker program, whichever is earlier. CW-2 status expires when the related CW-1 alien's status expires, on a CW-2 minor child's 18th birthday, when the alien violates status, or at the end of the program, whichever is earlier. No alien will be eligible for admission to the CNMI in CW status after the transitional worker program ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple specific events trigger expiration; beneficiaries and employers must track petition validity, revocation, termination, and program end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of inadmissibility for CNMI applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for CW-1 or CW-2 who is otherwise eligible and admissible to the United States, and who possesses appropriate documents demonstrating lawful presence in the CNMI, may be granted a waiver of inadmissibility under section 212(d)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act for certain grounds, as a matter of discretion, without additional form or fee. Appropriate documents include a valid unexpired passport and evidence of lawful presence (e.g., DHS I-94). Evidence may be provided by employer or family member or in other forms designated by USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary waiver process exists; evidence of lawful CNMI presence may accompany petitions or I‑539 filings and no extra fee/form required for the waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual report filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: During the validity period of the petition, an employer whose petition was approved for an employment start date on or after October 1, 2019 and for a validity period of six months or more, shall file a semiannual report, every six months after the petition validity start date up to and including the sixth month preceding the petition's validity end date. The semiannual report must be filed within a 60 day window surrounding the six month anniversary of the petition validity start date, with the filing window opening 30 days before and closing 30 days after the six month anniversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be filed in the form and containing such evidence as USCIS may direct to verify continuing employment and payment under the approved petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of semiannual reports and consequences of noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS may provide semiannual reports to other federal partners, including DOL, for investigative or other use. Failure to comply with semiannual report requirements may be a basis for revocation of an approved petition or for denial of subsequent petitions filed by the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance has enforcement consequences including revocation and denial of future filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer document retention and required records
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer must retain all documents and records in support of an approved petition and any semiannual report. Required evidence includes personnel records (name, CNMI address, age, domicile, citizenship, point of hire, approved contract termination date), payroll records (O*NET job classification; wage/salary; hours per week; gross compensation; itemized deductions; evidence of net payments made and received biweekly) and direct evidence of payment (receipts, canceled checks, deposit records). Petitioners must provide such documents and records to DHS and DOL at any time during the retention period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must preserve specified documentation and make it available on request; prepare payroll and personnel documentation consistent with these enumerated data points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer must retain documents and records until the date that is three years after the ending date of the petition validity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three‑year post‑petition validity retention period applies to all supporting documents and semiannual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify USCIS and general revocation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall immediately notify USCIS of any changes in the terms and conditions of employment of a beneficiary which may affect eligibility. To notify USCIS of such changes, an amended petition shall be filed when the petitioner continues to employ the beneficiary. If the petitioner no longer employs the beneficiary, the petitioner shall send a letter to the office at which the CW-1 petition was filed explaining the basis on which the specific CW-1 nonimmigrant is no longer employed. USCIS may revoke a petition at any time, even after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must proactively report employment changes and file amended petitions or explanatory letters as appropriate; USCIS has broad revocation authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate and automatic revocation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of any petition is immediately and automatically revoked if the petitioner ceases operations, files a written withdrawal of the petition, or the U.S. Department of Labor revokes the temporary labor certification upon which the petition is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain events cause automatic, non-appealable revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation on notice
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may send a notice of intent to revoke for good cause if it finds that: (1) the beneficiary is no longer employed by the petitioner in the capacity specified; (2) facts in the petition or labor certification application were not true, inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresented a material fact; (3) the petitioner violated terms and conditions of the approved petition; (4) the petitioner violated a requirement of paragraph (w); (5) the approval violated paragraph (w) or involved gross error; (6) the petitioner failed to maintain continuous employment, failed to pay the nonimmigrant, failed to timely file semiannual reports, committed other violations of terms and conditions, or ceased legitimate business operations; (7) the beneficiary did not apply for admission to the CNMI within 10 days after petition validity start if approved for consular processing; or (8) the employer failed to provide, within 21 business days of written request, originals or certified copies of petitions/notices/communications exchanged with federal agencies (excepting redacted sensitive employer info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated, specific grounds that justify a notice-of-intent-to-revoke; employers should maintain accurate records and timely compliance to avoid these grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation notice, rebuttal, and decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of intent to revoke shall state the grounds for revocation. The petitioner may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days of receipt of the notice. USCIS shall consider all relevant evidence presented in deciding whether to revoke the petition in whole or in part. If revoked in part, remainder of petition remains approved and a revised approval notice will be sent with the revocation notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners have a 30‑day opportunity to rebut; USCIS may partially revoke and issue revised approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition that has been revoked on notice in whole or in part may be appealed under part 103 of this chapter. Automatic revocations may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish revocation types: notice revocations are appealable; automatic revocations are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to DOL of revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will provide notice to DOL of CW-1 petition revocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency communication occurs when petitions are revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition and Form I-17 submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A school or school system seeking certification or recertification for attendance by F or M nonimmigrant students must file a petition with SEVP using SEVIS in accordance with procedures. The petition must state whether seeking F, M, or both, and must identify by name and address each location included in the petition (including any physical location where a nonimmigrant can attend classes). Certification and recertification petitions require that a complete Form I-17, Petition for Approval of School for Attendance by Nonimmigrant Student, bearing signatures, be included with supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEVIS/Form I‑17 and include all campus locations; signatures required; follow SEVP filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: School systems must list included schools and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition by a school system must include a list of the names and addresses of those schools included in the petition with the supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing as a school system, include each constituent school's identifying information and supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification obligations and legal attestation on Form I-17
rubrics_metrics.description: In submitting Form I-17, a school certifies that the designated school officials signing have read and understand DHS regulations relating to nonimmigrant students, change of classification, school certification and withdrawal, and that both the school and its DSOs intend to comply with these regulations at all times. Willful misstatements may constitute perjury (18 U.S.C. 1621).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatories carry legal attestation obligations; schools must ensure DSOs are familiar with cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible school types for F-1 certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The following schools may be certified for F-1 attendance: (A) colleges/universities awarding recognized bachelor's/master's/doctor/professional degrees; (B) community/junior colleges providing liberal arts/professional instruction awarding associate degrees; (C) seminaries; (D) conservatories; (E) academic high schools; (F) private elementary or middle schools; (G) institutions providing language training, liberal arts/fine arts/professional instruction, or multiple disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated institution types qualify for F‑1 certification; check category applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible school types for M-1 certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The following schools may be certified for M-1 attendance: (A) community/junior colleges providing vocational or technical training awarding associate degrees; (B) vocational high schools; (C) schools providing vocational or nonacademic training other than language training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M‑1 certification is limited to vocational/nonacademic institution types as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual F-1/M-1 certification and student intent rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A school may be certified for both F-1 and M-1 classification if it has both academic and vocational instruction. In that case, a student's classification depends on the student's primary intent — pursue liberal arts/fine arts/language/religion/professional study = F-1; primary intent to pursue vocational/technical training = M-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student primary intent determines classification when an institution is certified for both.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language training classification for vocational students
rubrics_metrics.description: A student whose primary intent is vocational or technical training who takes English language training at the same school solely to be able to understand the vocational course is classified as an M-1 nonimmigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited English coursework for vocational comprehension does not change M‑1 classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schools ineligible for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The following may not be certified for attendance by foreign students: (A) a home school; (B) a public elementary or middle school; or (C) an adult education program as defined by AEFLA if funded in whole or in part by certain federal/state/local funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain program types are categorically ineligible; review ineligible list before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for certification (bona fide school etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner, to be eligible for certification, must establish at the time of filing that it: (A) is a bona fide school; (B) is an established institution of learning or other recognized place of study; (C) possesses necessary facilities, personnel, and finances to conduct instruction in recognized courses; and (D) is, in fact, engaged in instruction in those courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish institutional legitimacy, facilities, staffing, finances, and active instruction at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification eligibility and compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for recertification at filing, the petitioner must establish that it remains eligible for certification and has complied during its previous period of certification or recertification with recordkeeping, retention, and reporting requirements and all other requirements of specified paragraphs (f), (g), (j), (k), and (l) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recertification requires demonstrable ongoing compliance with recordkeeping and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required licensure/approval/accreditation documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools petitioning for certification/recertification must submit licensure, approval, and accreditation documents. A charter will not be considered a license/approval/accreditation. Public schools must submit certification by an authorized public official that they are public educational institutions; private elementary/middle/secondary schools must submit certification that they meet state/local public educational requirements signed by authorized official; other petitioning schools must submit certification of license/approval/accreditation or, for veteran-eligible courses, a statement of recognition by the State approving agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate govt/agency certifications; charters alone are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: School operations information and required details
rubrics_metrics.description: Private schools not accredited by a nationally recognized accreditor must submit a school catalog if issued or a written statement containing: (i) size of physical facilities; (ii) nature of facilities for study/training; (iii) educational/vocational/professional qualifications of teaching staff; (iv) salaries of teachers; (v) attendance and scholastic grading policy; (vi) supervisory/consultative services available to students; and (vii) finances, including a certified accountant's last statement of net worth, income, and expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed operational and financial information if unaccredited; catalogs may substitute where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional evidence for vocational/business/language schools and research institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioning vocational, business, or language school, or an American institution of research recognized by the Secretary of Homeland Security, must submit evidence that its courses of study are accepted as fulfilling requirements for attainment of an educational, professional, or vocational objective, and have not been designated avocational or recreational through appropriate licensing/approval officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate occupational relevance and official recognition of programs; avoid programs designated as avocational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirements for unaccredited private elementary/middle schools
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioning private elementary, middle, or secondary school not accredited by a nationally recognized accreditor must submit evidence that attendance at the school satisfies the compulsory attendance requirements of the State and qualifies graduates for acceptance by schools of a higher educational level by public or accredited institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show state compliance and graduate transferability to higher-level schools when unaccredited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for unaccredited private higher education institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A private institution of higher learning not accredited by a nationally recognized accreditor must submit evidence that it confers recognized bachelor/master/doctor/professional/divinity degrees; or, if it does not confer such degrees, that its credits have been and are accepted unconditionally by at least three other public or accredited institutions of higher learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide degree-conferring evidence or third-party credit acceptance documentation for unaccredited higher ed institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner interview requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner or an authorized representative may be required to appear in person before or be interviewed by telephone by a DHS representative prior to adjudication. The interview will be conducted under oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to attend an in‑person or telephonic sworn interview as part of adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice service procedures and DSO contact obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices from SEVP to schools related to certification, recertification or out-of-cycle review will be served in accordance with specified procedures, generated and transmitted through SEVIS and/or by e-mail. The date of service is the date of transmission of the e-mail notice. DSOs must maintain current contact information, including current e-mail addresses, at all times. Failure to receive SEVP notices due to inaccurate DSO email addresses or spam filters is not grounds for appeal. The term 'in writing' means either a paper copy bearing original signatures or an electronic copy bearing electronic signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate SEVIS/DSO contact info; electronic service and signatures are valid; lack of receipt is not an appealable basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVP approval notification, validity, and recertification interval
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will notify the petitioner by updating SEVIS and by e-mail upon approval of a certification or recertification petition. The certification or recertification is valid only for the type of program and nonimmigrant classification specified in the approval notice. The certification must be recertified every two years and may be subject to out-of-cycle review at any time. Approval may be withdrawn in accordance with 8 CFR 214.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications are program/classification-specific and time‑limited (2 years); expect periodic and ad hoc reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting modifications to Form I-17 while SEVP-certified
rubrics_metrics.description: Any modification made by an SEVP-certified school on the Form I-17 at any time after certification and for the duration of a school's authorization to enroll F and/or M students must be reported to SEVP and will be processed by SEVP in accordance with specified provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Form I‑17 changes promptly and follow SEVP processing rules for modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic withdrawal for failure to submit recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve the school with a Notice of Intent to Withdraw (NOIW) 30 days prior to a school's SEVP certification expiration date if the school has not submitted a completed recertification petition. The school will be automatically withdrawn immediately if it has not submitted a completed recertification petition by the school's certification expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of recertification is mandatory; failure triggers automatic, immediate withdrawal and inability to enroll students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal on notice and consequences of failing to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a Withdrawal on Notice if it determines a school reviewed out-of-cycle has failed to sustain eligibility or comply with recordkeeping/retention/reporting requirements. When a school fails to file an answer to an NOIW within 30 days, SEVP will withdraw the school's certification and notify DSOs. A withdrawal for failure to respond to an NOIW may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to NOIW within 30 days to avoid non-appealable withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Denial for certification/recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Denial will be served to a school when SEVP denies a petition for certification or recertification. The notice will address appeals options. Schools denied recertification must comply with 8 CFR 214.4(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notices include appeal information; follow 214.4(i) requirements if denied recertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of SEVIS Access Termination Date and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of SEVIS Access Termination Date gives the official date for the school's denial or withdrawal to be final and SEVIS access to be terminated. In most situations, SEVP will not adjust a SEVIS access termination date when the appeals process has concluded and the denial or withdrawal has been upheld. The school will no longer be able to access SEVIS and SEVP will automatically terminate any remaining Active SEVIS records for that school on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination of SEVIS access is final on the termination date and leads to automatic termination of active student records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication approval conditions and reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of a petition for SEVP certification or recertification, the school is required to immediately report through SEVIS any change to its school information. Modification to school information listed in paragraph (h)(3) will require a determination of continued eligibility. Certification is valid only for the type/program specified and may be withdrawn; it is subject to review and reviewed every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After approval, continuously maintain up‑to‑date SEVIS information and report changes immediately to preserve eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication denial notification and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If SEVP denies a petition for certification or recertification, the petitioner will be notified of the reasons for the denial and appeal rights in accordance with 8 CFR part 103 and 8 CFR 214.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials include reasons and mechanisms for appeal; follow applicable CFR appeal procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student records retention and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An SEVP-certified school must keep records containing specific information and documents relating to each F-1 or M-1 student while the student is attending and until the school notifies SEVP that the student is no longer pursuing a full course of study. The school must keep a record of having complied with reporting requirements for at least three years after the student is no longer pursuing a full course of study. Required records include: identification of the school; identification of the student (including legal name changes, DOB, place of birth, citizenship, school ID); current physical address and mailing address if different; record of coursework (degree program/field, enrollment periods, course codes/titles, credits/contact hours, grades, withdrawals, GPA, cumulative credits); record of transfer credit accepted; academic status (suspension/dismissal/probation/withdrawal); practical training certifications; statement of graduation (degree/credential title, date conferred, program); termination date and reason; and documents referred to in paragraph (k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive, accurate, and accessible student records for the specified retention periods and be prepared to furnish transcripts and records to DHS upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response times for DHS information requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A DHS officer may request any or all data listed on student records. The school will have three work days to respond to any request for information concerning an individual student, and ten work days to respond for a class of students. The school will respond orally on the same day if DHS requests information on a student who is being held in custody, and DHS will provide a written notification after the fact if the school so desires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain readiness to produce records quickly: 3 business days for individual requests, 10 for class requests, immediate oral response if custody circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting timeline and events to report (21‑day rule and specified events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must update SEVIS with current information within 21 days of a change in specified school information and must report within 21 days any change of the information contained in student records or the occurrence of events including: student fails to maintain status or complete program; change of student's or dependent's legal name or U.S. address; any student who graduated early; disciplinary action as result of conviction; and other notifications requested by DHS. Additional requirements apply for F-1 students authorized for 24‑month OPT extension regarding employer information and employment end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely (21-day) reporting of enumerated events is mandatory; track student status and contact information constantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termly reporting of registration information (30‑day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each term or session, and no later than 30 days after the deadline for registering for classes, schools are required to report: whether the student has enrolled, dropped below a full course of study without prior authorization, or failed to enroll; the current address of each enrolled student; and the start date of the student's next session/term. For initial students, the start date is the program start date or report date; DSOs may choose a reasonable report date but not more than 30 days prior to classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report enrollment and address information each term within 30 days of registration deadlines; select reasonable report dates for initial students within the 30‑day limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update program completion date for factors affecting progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Any factors that influence the student's progress toward program completion (e.g., deferred attendance, authorized drop below, program extension) must be reflected by updating the program completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust program end dates promptly to reflect changes affecting progress toward completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative correction procedure for SEVIS errors
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where technological or computer problems on the part of SEVIS cause an error in the student's record, the DSO may request the SEVIS system administrator, without fee, to administratively correct the student's record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEVIS admin correction for system-caused errors; no fee for administrative corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and fee payment requirement for SEVP certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A school seeking SEVP certification must use SEVIS to file an electronic petition (which compiles the data for the Form I-17) and must submit the nonrefundable certification petition fee online as provided in 8 CFR 103.7(d)(2). The school must access the SEVP website to file and will be issued a temporary SEVIS user ID and password to complete and submit an electronic Form I-17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEVP filing is electronic via SEVIS; pay required nonrefundable fee online; use provided temporary credentials to submit Form I‑17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visit requirement and demonstration of regulatory knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will conduct a site visit for each petitioning school and its additional schools or campuses. SEVP will contact the school to arrange the site visit. The school must comply with and complete the visit within 30 days after SEVP contacts the school to arrange the visit, or the petition will be denied as abandoned. DSOs and school officials that have signed the school's Form I-17 must be able to demonstrate to DHS representatives how they obtain access to the regulations cited in the certification petition as part of the site visit. Paper or electronic access is acceptable. DSOs must be able to extract pertinent citations within the regulations related to their requirements and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for a site visit and be ready within 30 days; DSOs must have and be able to demonstrate access to and understanding of cited regulations.
